title: WEF ECP Fall 2026 methodology audit, depth 2
summary: Completed depth-2 pass that validates conservative pseudonymous-identity handling, adds R4228, and queues an official-role refresh.

classification_rules: A public handle remains a pseudonymous user unless independently supported identity evidence justifies a separate person-resolution review.
Exact username equality across platforms is a discovery signal, not identity proof.
Unresolved cross-platform collisions must remain separate entities and must not be merged.
Applicant status and portal-state claims are self-reported unless independently corroborated.
Candidate-facing Workday labels are tenant-configurable observations and must not be treated as universal stage semantics.
Private, gated, breach, residential, personal-contact, family and face-recognition data are out of scope.

findings.finding: Seed identity guardrails preserve pseudonymous users and reject username-only identity merges.
Official WEF Workday requisition R4228 exists and was absent from the July 27 depth-1 inventory.
Workday allows tenant-specific external recruiting label overrides.
Two additional New York ECP role titles are visible on the WEF company jobs discovery surface; official requisition IDs remain unresolved.

data.method: Repository methodology audit plus current official WEF Workday and Workday documentation review; secondary company-jobs discovery kept unresolved.
data.research_question: Are the seed packet's SOCMINT identity boundaries conservative enough, and what source-backed depth-2 recruitment-graph updates are available?

caveats: Two role titles remain discovery-only until official Workday IDs are resolved.

provenance.method: bounded public-source methodology audit and official requisition recursion

workflow.next_action: Run the queued official-role refresh without applicant identity expansion.
